title: Examples
text: mandelbrot.wasm renders Mandelbrot set memory, one byte per pixel holding number iterations point escaped. R reads bytes back matrix plots :  module arithmetic; R handles finished 43200-byte image.
code: mandel <- wasm_instantiate(example_module("mandelbrot")) w <- 240L h <- 180L maxiter <- 64L  mandel$render(0L, w, h, -2.4, -1.2, 0.9, 1.2, maxiter) iterations <- wasm_read(wasm_memory(mandel), 0, w * h, "u8") img <- matrix(iterations, nrow = w)  op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)) # Points that never escaped (the set itself) are black. colours <- c(hcl.colors(maxiter, "Inferno"), "black") image(img, col = colours, axes = FALSE, useRaster = TRUE) par(op)

code: wasm_imports(example_module("integrate")) #>   module name     kind         type #> 1   math    f function (f64) -> f64  integrator <- function(f) {   wasm_instantiate(     example_module("integrate"),     imports = list(math = list(f = wasm_func(f, params = "f64", results = "f64")))   ) }  integrator(sin)$trapezoid(0, pi, 1000L) #> [1] 1.999998 integrator(dnorm)$trapezoid(-1.96, 1.96, 1000L) #> [1] 0.9500039 calls <- 0 counted_exp <- function(x) {   calls <<- calls + 1   exp(-x^2) } integrator(counted_exp)$trapezoid(-3, 3, 200L) #> [1] 1.772415 calls #> [1] 201 picky <- integrator(function(x) if (x > 1) stop("x is too large") else x) err <- tryCatch(picky$trapezoid(0, 2, 10L), nanowasm_host_error = identity) conditionMessage(err) #> [1] "The R function imported as `math.f` failed: x is too large" conditionMessage(err$parent) #> [1] "x is too large"

what: SQL on a CSV file with SQLite
title: Real-world software
text: sqlite3.wasm official SQLite shell (version 3.53.4), compiled SQLite source wasi-sdk. Give directory SQL standard input, can query files directory: writable = TRUE can create database file, stays disk later runs: Without writable = TRUE program can’t change anything, can never see file outside directory given:
code: sqlite_module <- article_module("sqlite3")  sqlite <- function(sql, dir, db = ":memory:", writable = FALSE) {   # In a read-only directory SQLite can't create the lock file it uses on   # WASI, so open database files as immutable there.   if (!writable && db != ":memory:") db <- paste0("file:", db, "?immutable=1")   wasm_run(     sqlite_module,     args = c("-csv", "-header", db),     stdin = sql,     dirs = dir,     writable = writable,     env = c(HOME = "/nowhere") # no ~/.sqliterc to look for   ) }  data_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "cars") dir.create(data_dir, showWarnings = FALSE) cars <- cbind(model = rownames(mtcars), mtcars) write.csv(cars, file.path(data_dir, "mtcars.csv"), row.names = FALSE)  res <- sqlite(c(   ".import mtcars.csv cars",   "SELECT cyl, count(*) AS n, round(avg(mpg), 1) AS mpg, max(hp) AS max_hp",   "FROM cars GROUP BY cyl ORDER BY cyl;" ), dir = data_dir) read.csv(text = res$stdout) #>   cyl  n  mpg max_hp #> 1   4 11 26.7     97 #> 2   6  7 19.7    175 #> 3   8 14 15.1    335 res <- sqlite(c(   ".import mtcars.csv cars",   "CREATE INDEX cars_by_mpg ON cars(mpg);" ), dir = data_dir, db = "cars.db", writable = TRUE) res$status #> [1] 0 list.files(data_dir) #> [1] "cars.db"    "mtcars.csv"  # A later, read-only run queries it. res <- sqlite(   "SELECT model, mpg FROM cars ORDER BY mpg DESC LIMIT 3;",   dir = data_dir, db = "cars.db" ) read.csv(text = res$stdout) #>            model  mpg #> 1 Toyota Corolla 33.9 #> 2       Fiat 128 32.4 #> 3   Lotus Europa 30.4 sqlite("DELETE FROM cars;", dir = data_dir, db = "cars.db")$stderr #> [1] "Error near line 1: attempt to write a readonly database\n" sqlite(".import ../../etc/passwd pw", dir = data_dir)$stderr #> [1] "line 1: cannot open \"../../etc/passwd\"\n"

what: A C library on an R matrix
title: Real-world software
text: every module program. terrain.wasm small C library, built WASI “reactor”: main, exports functions, plus alloc() release() R ask space memory. hillshade() computes landscape look lit north-west, classic way draw relief. volcano’s cells 10 m wide; passing 5 exaggerates relief twice, makes easier see:
code: terrain <- wasm_instantiate(article_module("terrain"), wasi = wasm_wasi()) wasm_exports(terrain) #>          name     kind                                      type #> 1 _initialize function                                  () -> () #> 2       alloc function                              (i32) -> i32 #> 3   hillshade function (i32, i32, i32, i32, f64, f64, f64) -> () #> 4      memory   memory                                     min 2 #> 5     release function                               (i32) -> () #> 6       slope function           (i32, i32, i32, i32, f64) -> ()  # Run one of the library's grid functions on matrix z. grid_fn <- function(fun, z, ...) {   mem <- wasm_memory(terrain)   n <- length(z)   input <- terrain$alloc(8L * n)   output <- terrain$alloc(8L * n)   on.exit({     terrain$release(input)     terrain$release(output)   })   wasm_write(mem, input, as.vector(z), "f64")   wasm_call(terrain, fun, input, output, nrow(z), ncol(z), ...)   matrix(wasm_read(mem, output, n, "f64"), nrow = nrow(z)) }  shade <- grid_fn("hillshade", volcano, 5, 315, 45) slope <- grid_fn("slope", volcano, 10) summary(as.vector(slope)) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>   0.000   6.379  13.520  14.330  21.191  43.032 op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5)) image(volcano, col = terrain.colors(50), axes = FALSE, main = "Elevation") image(shade, col = grey.colors(50, 0, 1), axes = FALSE, main = "Hillshade") contour(volcano, add = TRUE, drawlabels = FALSE, col = "#00000040") par(op)

title: Conditions signalled by nanowasm — nanowasm-conditions
text: nanowasm_invalid_object: object longer points live module instance, example saveRDS() / readRDS() round trip. nanowasm_validation_error: bytes valid WebAssembly module. nanowasm_link_error: module instantiated imports given. missing field lists missing imports. nanowasm_argument_error: value passed R fit function's signature. subclass nanowasm_precision_error used i64 result represented exactly double. nanowasm_unsupported: function uses type nanowasm pass R WebAssembly (funcref, externref, v128). nanowasm_trap: WebAssembly code trapped. trap_id names trap ("div_by_zero", "unreachable", "out_of_bounds_memory_access", ...) detail holds interpreter's message. Subclasses: nanowasm_stack_exhausted (call value stack limit) nanowasm_out_of_bounds (memory table access bounds). trap also says happened: func name function trapped, backtrace names functions call stack, innermost first (64), depth full depth stack. Names come module's name section (wat2wasm's --debug-names, compiler's debug information), else exports imports, else func[N]. Timeouts errors imported R functions carry fields. nanowasm_memory_limit: instance reached memory limit (see wasm_limits()), interpreter allocate memory. nanowasm_timeout: call ran longer time limit. elapsed limit seconds. nanowasm_reentry_error: instance called already running call. nanowasm_runtime_error: failure inside interpreter. --bounds wasm_read() wasm_write() calls signal nanowasm_out_of_bounds , subclass nanowasm_argument_error. Pressing Ctrl-C call signals R's usual interrupt condition. WASI program calls exit() stops WebAssembly call nanowasm_host_error whose parent class nanowasm_wasi_exit exit status; wasm_wasi_start() wasm_run() turn returned status.

title: Instantiate a module and call its functions — wasm_instantiate
text: Calls scalar: argument one value, matched function's parameter types. i32 accepts integer, double holding whole number \([-2^{31}, 2^{32})\); values \(2^{31}\) taken unsigned bit pattern. i32 results integers. NA_integer_ shares bits \(-2^{31}\), two value WebAssembly. i64 accepts whole number magnitude \(2^{53}\), i64 results doubles. result double represent exactly signals nanowasm_precision_error rather rounded. f32 f64 accept numbers, return doubles. function results returns NULL invisibly, one single result returns length-one vector, one several results returns unnamed list. title: Resource limits for an instance — wasm_limits

title: Resource limits for an instance — wasm_limits
text: memory caps everything interpreter allocates instance: linear memories, tables, globals stacks running calls. memory.grow exceed fails inside WebAssembly (returning -1, specification requires). allocation exceed signals nanowasm_memory_limit error. frames maximum call depth, stack maximum number value-stack cells (4 bytes ). Exceeding either signals nanowasm_stack_exhausted error. timeout wall-clock time single call (including start function instantiation) may run, seconds. Exceeding signals nanowasm_timeout error. checked every 50 milliseconds execution. Pressing Ctrl-C (Esc) interrupts running call regardless limits, R code. call stopped limit interrupt may leave instance's memory globals partly updated. instance stays usable, whether state still makes sense depends module.

code: wasm_limits() #> <nanowasm_limits> #>   memory:  256 MiB #>   frames:  10,000 #>   stack:   1,000,000 cells #>   timeout: none wasm_limits(memory = 16 * 2^20, timeout = 1) #> <nanowasm_limits> #>   memory:  16 MiB #>   frames:  10,000 #>   stack:   1,000,000 cells #>   timeout: 1 s  mod <- wasm_module(system.file("extdata", "fib.wasm", package = "nanowasm")) inst <- wasm_instantiate(mod, limits = wasm_limits(timeout = 0.5)) try(inst$fib(40L)) #> Error in inst$fib(40L) :  #>   The WebAssembly call was stopped after 0.5 seconds, its time limit.

title: Access an instance's linear memory — wasm_memory
code: mod <- wasm_module(system.file("extdata", "sum.wasm", package = "nanowasm")) inst <- wasm_instantiate(mod) mem <- wasm_memory(inst) mem #> <nanowasm_memory> `memory`: 1 page (64 KiB)  # Ask the module for room for 5 doubles, fill it, and sum it. x <- c(1.5, 2.5, 3, 4, 5) ptr <- inst$alloc(8L * length(x)) wasm_write(mem, ptr, x, "f64") inst$sum_f64(ptr, length(x)) #> [1] 16 wasm_read(mem, ptr, 5, "f64") #> [1] 1.5 2.5 3.0 4.0 5.0  next_free <- wasm_write_string(mem, 1024, "héllo") wasm_read_string(mem, 1024) #> [1] "héllo" wasm_read(mem, 1024, next_free - 1024, "u8") #> [1] 104 195 169 108 108 111   0

title: nanowasm 0.0.0.9000
text: Development version, heading first release (0.1.0). wasm_module() loads validates WebAssembly module raw vector .wasm file; wasm_validate() checks . wasm_exports() wasm_imports() list module provides needs. wasm_instantiate() creates instance (running start function), wasm_call() inst$name(...) calls exported functions, converting i32, i64, f32 f64 values R. wasm_memory() gives access instance’s linear memory: wasm_read() / wasm_write() typed vectors, wasm_read_string() / wasm_write_string() UTF-8 strings, wasm_memory_size() / wasm_memory_grow(). wasm_global() reads sets exported globals. Modules can import R functions: wrap wasm_func() pass wasm_instantiate(imports = ). R function caller argument can reach calling instance’s memory. WASI: wasm_run() runs programs compiled WebAssembly System Interface (preview 1), wasm_wasi() / wasm_instantiate(wasi = ) / wasm_wasi_start() give finer control. Programs get arguments environment pass, standard streams (console, captured discarded), R’s clocks random numbers, files inside directories grant, read-unless writable = TRUE. wasm_stats() reports instance’s memory use (current, peak limit) much work done (runs, function calls, calls imports, branches). wasm_limits() bounds instance’s memory, call depth, value stack time per call; Ctrl-C interrupts running call. trap names function happened , condition carries WebAssembly call stack (func, backtrace, depth). Every failure classed condition (nanowasm_trap, nanowasm_timeout, nanowasm_host_error, …); see ?nanowasm-conditions. Modules run bundled toywasm interpreter (v76.0.0), system WebAssembly runtime needed. vignette("nanowasm") walks API, example modules add.wasm, fib.wasm, sum.wasm, log.wasm, hello-wasi.wasm cat-wasi.wasm installed extdata/.
